inputs.xtext_rule_text:
fragment SenderReceiverPart returns SysML::ActionUsage :
	'via' ownedRelationship += NodeParameterMember 
	  ( 'to' ownedRelationship += NodeParameterMember )?
	| ownedRelationship += EmptyParameterMember
	  'to' ownedRelationship += NodeParameterMember
;

notes: re-scoped from the shared unit to sysml alone (ADR-0015)
decision: A transcription of SysML 8.2.2.17.4. The clause and the Xtext state this production identically, so there is nothing to weigh. The two alternatives are the two ways a send names its ends: 'via' a sender, optionally also 'to' a receiver; or no sender at all — an EmptyParameterMember, which contributes no tokens — and 'to' a receiver. The second alternative is why `send x to y` binds `y` as the receiver rather than the sender, and why the parameter positions come out the same in both spellings. This is the production SendNode's own clause line misspells as SendReceiverPart; see the deviation of that name.

evidence.note: States the production; the rule is its transcription. The pack flags this clause as malformed, but the defect is in TriggerExpression (SYSML21-401) and not in this production.
Line 21 `then send new S() to b;` takes the second alternative: no sender, `b` as the receiver after 'to'.
Line 60 `entry send new CallGiveItems("All the items") via apisp.APIS_HTTP;` takes the first alternative with the 'to' part absent.
Line 1328 `do send new IgnitionCmd (ignitionOnOff=IgnitionOnOff::on) via handPort` is the first alternative again, as a transition effect.
Second opinion. Identical to the clause.
Records that SendNode's clause line references this production under a name defined nowhere.
